records.subject: SOC
records.title: Introduction to Sociology
records.description: Introduction to the discipline of sociology: Concepts and methods used in the inquiry into the social world.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Social Problems
records.description: The structure of social institutions and cultural factors that constitute threats to society (crime, poverty, discrimination, drugs, family violence).

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Social Psychology of Communication
records.description: Use of social psychological principles to communicate effectively with diverse audiences.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Murder and Mass Mayhem in American Society
records.description: Similarities and differences in murder and mass mayhem within the US and between US and other nations.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Society and Technology
records.description: Role of technology in social evolution; social impacts and shaping of technology.  Recommended preparation:  SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Sociology of Sport
records.description: Sociological study of sport in America.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Perspectives on Disability
records.description: Historical, international, socioeconomic, ethical and personal perspectives on disability; individual choices, societal values, and social responsibility.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: The Sociology of Sex, Relationships, and Marriage
records.description: Social and personal factors in mate selection; the sociology of sexuality; development of gender roles; and intimate relationships and marriage. (Crosslisted course offered as SOC 251, WGSS 251.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Intersections of Race, Class, Gender, Sexuality, and Dis/ability
records.description: Study of intersections among race, class, gender, sexuality, and dis/ability through case studies; experiences in interdisciplinary methods. (Crosslisted course offered as WGSS 300, ENGLISH 310, SOC 300.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Contemporary Masculinities
records.description: Analysis of the development of masculinity in its biological and cultural forms. (Crosslisted course offered as WGSS 302, SOC 302.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Preparing for Internships and Sociology Careers
records.description: Explore career options, develop professional materials, and learn strategies for internship and job searching, networking, and interviewing; emphasis is placed on connecting academic training to real-world opportunities and career paths.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Development of Social Theory
records.description: Foundations of sociological theory; introduction to original works of early social theorists. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Visual Presentation and Data Management in Social Science
records.description: Investigate and communicate with social science data; techniques of visual data display using Excel and other tools.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Research Methods in Sociology
records.description: Designing, conducting, and reporting social research.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Introduction to Social Research
records.description: Methods of collecting data; surveys, experiments, field observations; organization and interpretation of data; reading social research findings.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Understanding the Social World with Data
records.description: Making sense of data and storytelling with numbers. Gain career-related skills in analyzing, interpreting, and reporting on social data.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: America's Changing Population: Challenges and Strategies
records.description: Introduction to population studies and to measurements of fertility, mortality, and migration; study of impacts of populations changes on contemporary social issues (e.g., mass incarceration, poverty, teen pregnancy, environment).

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Sustainability and Society
records.description: The study of human-environment relationships and the connections between environmental, economic, and social systems.  Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Science, Power and Human Values
records.description: Recent developments in the sociological study of science and scientific knowledge through cultural, commercial, and political perspectives.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Medical Sociology
records.description: Study of the societal dimensions of health and medicine: social determinants of health.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Shopping and Society
records.description: Consumption and its impacts on the environment and society.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Sociology of Food
records.description: Theoretical, historical, and empirical issues of food and agriculture in the United States including social, political, and economic aspects. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Climate Change in Your Lifetime
records.description: Reflections on personal experiences with climate change, climate politics and policy, scientific uncertainty, and more

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Environmental Inequality and Justice
records.description: Causes and consequences of poor and minoritized communities' uneven exposure to environmental risks and hazards; social and political solutions that address community level environmental inequities.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Social Inequality
records.description: Causes and consequences of social inequality in contemporary America. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Inclusive Workplace Leadership
records.description: For upper-division students, development of leadership skills necessary for careers in a diverse workplace.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Urban Poverty
records.description: Historical context and current debates on US urban poverty including public policy, employment and education, and gender, race, and ethnicity. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Sociology of Professions and Occupations
records.description: Social organization of work in America including historical and contemporary trends, bureaucracy, gender/racial inequality, technological affects, work/family relations. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Sociology of Education
records.description: Examination of how educational institutions are influenced by other social forces, how school practices affect individual outcomes and how race/class/gender shape educational opportunity. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Sociology of Race, Ethnicity, and Immigration
records.description: Racial and ethnic categories and experiences of specific racial, ethnic, and immigrant groups.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Social Psychology
records.description: Attitude changes, conformity, interpersonal relations, groups and social influences explored to give a coherent view of social psychology. Recommended preparation: PSYCH 105 or SOC 101. (Crosslisted course offered as PSYCH 350, SOC 350.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: The Family
records.description: Family system and its interaction patterns; family formation and dissolution; marital and partner relations, divorce, sexuality, parenting, work-family balance. Recommended preparation: SOC 101. (Crosslisted course offered as SOC 351, WGSS 351.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Youth and Society
records.description: Social issues facing youth; youth and social institutions of education, employment, family, criminal justice system, and politics.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Growing Up and Growing Older
records.description: Aging as a lifelong process; behavior, personality competencies, social relations changes over the life course; historical, social structural, demographics, contextual influences.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Beliefs, Norms, and Values
records.description: Sources and consequences of beliefs, norms, and values.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Giving
records.description: Giving that contributes to flourishing societies; philanthropy, volunteering, cooperation, and altruism.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Social Deviance
records.description: A survey of the sociology of deviance. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Criminology
records.description: Crime measurement, theories of crime, the correlates of crime, and specific types of crime such as white-collar and drug crime. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Juvenile Delinquency
records.description: Sociological perspectives on delinquency; delinquent gangs and subcultures; delinquency causation and control; law and its enforcement: juvenile justice and corrections. Recommended preparation: SOC 101.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Law and Society
records.description: Intersection of legal and social systems.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Juvenile Justice and Corrections
records.description: History, philosophy, legal process, performance, and outcomes of the juvenile justice and corrections systems. (Crosslisted course offered as CRM J 365, SOC 367.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Drugs and Society
records.description: Social issues in drug use and addiction; drug policy.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: The Sociology of Film
records.description: The social, economic, and political factors that influence film production and the impact of films on American culture.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Media, Culture, and Society
records.description: The production of popular culture by media organizations and its effects on society.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Environmental Economics and Policy
records.description: Application of economic principles to environmental issues, especially the application of economic theory to environmental valuation, the regulation of pollution, and different ways to achieve sustainable development. (Crosslisted course offered as ECONS 326, SOC 375.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Sociology of Gender
records.description: Construction and maintenance of gender and gender inequality in American society. Recommended preparation: SOC 101. (Crosslisted course offered as SOC 384, WGSS 384.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer Studies
records.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of issues related to gender and sexuality, explored transhistorically and cross-culturally, including race, class and age differences. (Crosslisted course offered as WGSS 385, SOC 385.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Gender and Work
records.description: Gender and inequality at work including occupational segregation, wage inequality and balancing work and family. (Crosslisted course offered as SOC 390, WGSS 390.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Globalization
records.description: Structural foundations of global social change; theories of intersocietal interactions and interdependencies.  Recommended preparation:  SOC 101.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Human Issues in International Development
records.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of complex interaction in the context of colonial and post-colonial development.  (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 418, POL S 418, SOC 418.)

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Quantitative Techniques in Sociology II
records.description: Probability theory, sampling distributions, random variables, matrix approaches to statistical techniques, calculus for statistics and computer applications.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Corrections
records.description: History, facilities, processes, strategies for the correction and punishment of offenders, analysis of concepts of prevention and control of crime.  Recommended preparation:  SOC 101.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Geographic Information Systems in Health and Social Sciences
records.description: Utilizing Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and mapping tools to examine and visualize epidemiological and social science data; assess public health, social, and policy issues including obesity, cardiovascular disease, and drug use; explore how this work can be applied to interventions. Required preparation must include a college-level statistics course.  (Crosslisted course offered as NEP 462/562, SOC 462/562.) Credit not granted for both NEP 462/562 and SOC 462/562.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Addictive Behavior Among Diverse Populations
records.description: Overview of social, cultural, and historical perspectives on dealing with addictive behavior. Recommended preparation: SOC 101, PSYCH 105, or CRM J 101. (Crosslisted course offered as PSYCH 468, CRM J 468, SOC 468.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Social Movements
records.description: Social movement processes and social change in historical and contemporary societies.  Recommended preparation:  SOC 101.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Internship
records.description: Work experience related to undergraduate major and career interests.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Internship Capstone
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: SOC 310 or concurrent enrollment; junior standing.
records.description: Self-initiated supervised work experience in an approved campus or community setting.  Recommended preparation: SOC 317 or 320, and SOC 321 or CRM J 321.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Capstone Research Practicum
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: SOC 317, SOC 320, PSYCH 312, or CRM J 311, or concurrent enrollment in any; admitted to the major in Sociology; junior standing.
records.description: Hands-on experience in selection of a social problem, review of literature, identifying data sources, developing methodology and reporting results.  Senior standing recommended.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Research Assistantship
records.description: Supervised experience in current research by departmental faculty.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: SOC
records.title: Special Problems
records.description: Independent study conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include independent research studies in technical or specialized problems; selection and analysis of specified readings; development of a creative project; or field experiences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
